tips.comment: Showed a hint of ability over hurdles but made a promising debut over fences at Market Rasen in a race which is working out. Up in grade but can only improve and will do for me with Sam on board again.

Gats And Co comes into this race in excellent form after a convincing win last time out, proving his stamina over staying trips like this one. His recent victory at 3m2f boosts his credentials. With Connor Brace aboard and renewed confidence, he has everything in his favour to score again in this competitive handicap.

I can see Palacio and Seeyouinmydreams taking on each other in front. Hopefully, Alan King's 7-year-old, a strong stayer at two miles, can mop up the pieces. He won at last year's Sandown Finale meeting, the Class 2 novice handicap hurdle, a much better race than this.
See You In My Dreams can upset the favorite here for Cobden and Nicholls. The favorite has the better form, but there might just be a bit more to come from the former champion trainer's yard.

Could be very interesting at this price. Not been seen since a poor run last May. But the plus is the stable is in cracking form, and reverting to hurdles might be a plus along with being fresh for this.
Ballybreeze won by over 4L when last out in March. I would expect to see him thereabouts again while up just 5 lbs.

Do You Know What I Mean is sent out again by Dan Skelton pretty quickly after a recent win in the aim of getting a bit of a lead on WM. This can be another one, although the market leader is a real danger.
Three-runner race, and this one has to be considered here. The drop back in trip should prove ideal, and with cheekpieces fitted, it should go well.

Courageous Strike was easily the best of these on the flat, having won twice and been placed on 5 occasions in Ireland. He joined Paul Nicholls last month and made an encouraging debut over hurdles when 2nd at Ffos Las 3 weeks ago. That was over 2m4f, which he possibly found too far. This drop back to 2m looks ideal, and he looks the most likely winner.

The model I run suggests King Of Records can win this race. Much higher RPR compared to the rest of the field, steps out carrying similar weight to the rest of the field, and Charlie Deutch picks up the reins. The biggest threat here is Roadshow, who's running his second race since a wind op.
Harry Cobden teams up with Faye Bramley here on Amancio, who looked good for their second last time out. Under a nice weight here, they have an advantage over the market rival.

Dalamoi has been running well in point-to-points, winning three on the bounce with one of the runners-up franking that form. Comes here with a bit to prove on previous C&D runs, but on ratings is a serious contender.

The model I run suggests Lahinch Wave can get over the line first in this one. Previous outing (a long time ago now) came first. Steps out for the first time in a hood to aid concentration. Main concern is the length of time between the last run and this.
Sangiovese won well last time out, and although up 5 pounds, is fairly unexposed and probably still ahead of the handicapper. Looked like it will stay and can justify favouritism here.
Course and distance winner last June from this same mark of 110, his 5th run on the bounce. Has had a breathing operation since his last 2 disappointing runs. Chance if fit enough.
Constant Friday is off a very low weight here and looked like it needed the run when finishing third. Has strong each-way claims.

Mortens Leam has been running consistently well despite being 13 years old, and the form seems strong enough to compete at this level of race. Third to Siam Park, form figures of 2-1-1-2. The most recent runner-up effort was to the talented Shakeyatailfeather, trained by Dan Skelton. Also, beat Cloudy Wednesday on the penultimate run, who's won again since. Has strong course form - 2 wins, twice runner-up, and 3rd place from the last 8 runs here.

Stable in form, and this should have more to give in handicaps after a confidence-boosting win in an Ayr novice LTO. His 2nd to Roadlesstravelled earlier in the season reads well, with that horse rated 135+, so this unchanged mark of 112 looks very workable.
Valadon made no impression last time out over 2m, but this extra 5f could just be what is needed and can get back to some form. Market suggested could go close.

The handicapper may well have the measure of a few of these, whereas Kingston Gent has just had the one start in handicaps, which came on heavy at Exeter last time. His previous run at Taunton at this trip was on good to soft, and he was beaten just six lengths then. His pointing win came over 2m4f good, and this will be his first run under rules on similar ground. Looks likely to be seriously asked what he can do today. He could be good enough to win, and his price offers EW thief value.

Sunshine Diamond makes a handicap debut after winning twice in novice/maiden company between Ireland and the UK. Seeks a hat trick and has been given top weight for the handicap debut. The form of those wins has been boosted, beating Shakeyatailfeather (now seeking a hat trick) and beating Marv Michael by 6 lengths (since won twice in Ireland). Both wins were on good ground and have clocked up good speed ratings. NAP

He has won 3 times over hurdles, including a win at this track in February. He hasn't finished any lower than 3rd in his 3 runs since that win, and he has been dropped 1lb since his 2nds he recently encountered, which could be the drop he needs to return to winning ways.

CHURCHILLS BOY is clearly on a good mark. That may be with good reason of course , but he is a winner at this venue and that counts for plenty around this quirky circuit. He has presumably had his issues , but if straight today he could surprise.

I think we can excuse the last three runs from REBEL INTENTIONS as one was over fences and two were in a higher grade. He's now only a pound above the last winning mark, runs well fresh, and drops back to more beatable company. Could pick off some of these and get involved if matching the form when last seen at around this sort of handicap.
Has been inconsistent but does go well at this track, winning this time last year over this course and distance, and is 1lb lower now. Ran well on latest start over a shorter trip. Sets this up well.
Ferret Jeeter is looking strong in the market. Although hasn't run well, comes here very well treated and off a low mark. Has to be respected.
Irish point winner who showed she's as good as ever when winning a 9-runner race at Hereford 10 weeks ago. Lightly raced and should have more to offer.

Vendant went well here over 2m5f in January when 2nd, beaten a neck. Upped in class next time and not disgraced over 3m1f at Plumpton. Pulled up when bled from the nose last time, so has to be forgiven. Went well on good to firm over 3m in a point, and the lightly raced 7-year-old looks capable of making the frame at least if all's well this time.

Tedwin Hills, normally a sound jumper, had the race in his grasp last time (Ffos Las, good to soft) until a blunder 3 out caused the rider to lose his reins and pull up. Kept to the same trip tonight and on slightly better ground, a winner on good, he should be putting in another big effort and may take some catching.

Tommy Dillion has been struggling to finish his last few races, and only one he didn't finish fifth. But he is off a fairly low weight here. A change in trip and the ground may just be enough for a placing at decent odds.

Race 7 at Doncaster today is a Handicap (Class 4) for 3-year-olds over 1,009 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old filly Fiorella Princess from the Lemos de Souza yard, and she will be ridden by Callum Shepherd. This daughter of Sands Of Mali came close to winning her second when a photo finish third on her latest start. She has proven ability, and her second win should not be far off, with today presenting a good chance. She must be respected here.

ALONDRA was a tad green when last seen at Doncaster 6f, but she's improved somewhat since then, and I like her chances today. The Sergei Prokofiev filly stuck to her task at Southwell earlier in the month, and she will want fast ground on a galloping track to boost her chances; there could be more to come while racing over the minimum trip.
Stable in form with 5 winners from the last 10 runners. Selection has been running on AW, winning the penultimate start back in January and probably needed the run last month. EW chance.

Smart on the flat, rated 100. Four starts over hurdles, winning his last three races. He had a nice prep two weeks ago, never in trouble when winning a useful novice hurdle under a big weight, winning by 2L and sprinting through the line. No problem with the better ground. An opening handicap mark of 128 could be lenient.

Where Red and Blue look to have an each-way chance at a big price in this handicap. He went very well at this track in the Imperial Cup last time, and with a slightly more patient ride, could run into a place.

The 7-year-old has taken well to fences this campaign, progressing nicely, form 2022-21. He won a decent-looking handicap over this C/D last time out, winning by 6L and another 10L back to the 3rd. He’ll be fresh after a 7-week break. Still on a handy low mark despite a rise in the weights.

Insurrection looked like he may turn into a high-class horse in his early days but has been slightly disappointing. He is now getting his act together, and with the Paul Nicholls horses finishing the season in good form, he holds a good chance here.

Moved from Patrick Neville's Yorkshire yard to flat trainer Dylan Cunha, the combination of new surroundings and tactics have certainly done the trick. A front-running good jumper, this place looks made for him and is certainly worth an each-way bet at his overpriced odds.

Pretty obvious here, but he looks to only have one serious challenger. Presuming it's not too quick a turnaround from Aintree, he should be picking this up really. Mullins has every reason to want this to win, and I doubt Ricci would be letting him run without a serious chance.

The 10-year-old has the second highest rating in this Grade 2 chase. Suited by the better ground. He has 2 wins from 2 this campaign. He won a Grade 1 by 10 lengths last time out. He’s had a nice 10-week break, and freshness can win the day.

Top Irish trainer Willie Mullins is favourite to win the UK jumps top-trainer championship for the second season running. Recent Aintree winner Gentleman De Mee can add more prize money to the Mullins pot.

Gaelic Warrior is class but unpredictable, and I can't get away from the thinking Pic D'Orhy is suited by flat tracks, so happy to pass both over. Le Patron has saved his best for Sandown, making all to win a novice handicap here by 10L and then following up by claiming the Grade 1 Henry VIII Novice Chase on heavy ground. Rhythm is so vital around here as the jumping can really be tested, and with the cheekpieces fitted, I wouldn't be surprised to see him bounce off from the front to put the rest under pressure. The yard is in good form, and he seems unlikely to be inconvenienced by the quick ground, having won a handicap earlier this season by 7L on good to soft from a mark of 146. Bare form leaves him plenty to find with the market principals, but unlike them, he's proven at the track and can spring a small surprise.

The 6yo was 4th in this race last year, beaten on the run-in, a couple of jumping errors not helping that day. Four runs this campaign, going close in Grade 2 and Grade 1 company. Ground against him last time out but he has been kept fresh with a 2 month break. Rated to be a big player.

Harpers Brook is a talented individual who unfortunately has his own ideas about the game. Hopefully, if they go a good gallop, which seems likely, he can run up the hill and grab some place money at huge odds.
Last year's winner of this race, Minella Cocooner, ran well in this year's Grand National despite his saddle slipping. He looks a spring horse and can go well today.

Just five starts over fences for the 7yo, still unexposed. He was a good 4th of 18 at the festival and has no problem with this 3m 4f trip. He’s had a six week break to freshen up. I like the fact that his best RPR rating came on better ground during Nov in a useful Listed contest, beaten 1/2L, splitting two rivals rated 147 and 154. His current handicap mark of 142 should give him every chance.

Victtorino just doesn't seem to perform when going left-handed, but he has a very good record going right-handed, as is the case here. He has put up some sterling performances this year on right-handed tracks such as Ascot, and Venetia Williams showed some signs of a return to form over the last day or so.

This horse won the Eider Chase at Newcastle in great style 2 starts ago. Got bogged down in the mud at Uttoxeter last time out, and although some way out of the weights, can reward each-way support in this race.

Three runs this year for the 5yo, after coming off a 10 month break. Decent maiden hurdle form, 2nd of 21 then 1st of 17. Runner-up in a novice hurdle last time out, losing out on the run in to a good yardstick and he did lose a shoe. Every chance off an opening handicap of 133, no problem with the 20f trip and better ground.

Trilby is a sprinter on the up and in very good form. A good combination when seeking out winners. It's a bit of a surprise his trainer Sam England has chosen to come here for this race. I guess he likes the look of the 26k first prize.

Fairly consistent last season barring Ayr Gold Cup flop when doing too much too soon. 5th at York latest can be upgraded having led with 6 forcing the pace and collapsed as a result in the last furlong. Looks the only real front runner here and will probably be able to come over from bad draw in 11 to take the lead, set the fractions, and kick on to win. Won seasonal debut last year and Kevin Ryan going well. Oisin takes the ride for the 3rd time having won both previous starts together. Gelded since last season provides encouragement too.

Likely to be the classiest horse in here, and doubtful the top weight would blunt that too much. Pace around him, Gorak likely to go forward. Low draws over the 7f course here are always favored and should be able to get a nice tow in and pick them off up the run-in. CD winner last season and had run well on seasonal debut the time before. Went on to win at Royal Ascot. Gelded since last season, encouraging, and Ed Walker going to 27% currently with a number not far off. Well overpriced at 6s, 4 places available. Myal main danger if going forward, however, seemingly shows best with juice in the ground.
This horse tends to run his best races in the early part of the season. Has run well here in the past and looks fairly handicapped at an attractive each way price

This horse normally comes on for his first run of the season. Has won here in the past and after having a run should be ready to put his best foot forward. He is a huge price which underestimates his ability.

A very open-looking sprint where Ziggys Queen appeals as a solid each-way bet at 14/1 with 5 places up for grabs. She had excuses on her seasonal reappearance and should also be fitter for that. She ran some solid races last year in better races off higher marks and has a good high draw here.

Most likely to be prominent/lead, which suits Ripon. Race fit. Won over CD by 3.25L off 80, so 82 shouldn't be too far of a stretch and has run well up to 88/89. 6yo now, with the 5/6-year-olds always performing better at this stage in the season before the 4yo reach peak maturity. Ground fine and should run a nice race.

Manila Scouse's form on paper may seem off putting however looks can be deceiving and a deeper analysis of this individual tells a whole different story his last couple of races of his 2024 campaign where in very big field handicaps where he can be excused and was last seen making his seasonal reappearance at Pontefract 18 days ago where finishing last of 10 however a line is best drawn over that run as he most certainly was in need of the outing and he did have a wide trip throughout and dirited even wider out turning for the home straight resulting in him losing his pace and eventually got left behind but that has at least got a run into him and arrives here fitter from the outing and in very good heart operating back on a more lenient mark that being 85 just 2lb above his last winning mark and this mark is within range likely to better positioned in this 7 horse scenario that should suit well Manila Scouse can bounce back to form with jockey Amie Waugh taking off 3lb which only enhances his good looking claims here
